_what: Human-read NET sizes for Sam's Club rows whose pack size the builder can only back-solve as linePrice / unitPrice. Sam's prints unitPrice rounded to the cent, so a derived size carries a relative error of 0.005/unitPrice (7.1% at $0.07/oz, 10% at $0.05/oz) and the board was ranking that quotient as an exact number. A hint here replaces the quotient with a real reading.
_rules: NEVER GUESS A NUMBER. net_oz / net_floz / net_lb / net_ct is read off the product label or the PDP specifications, and 'source' says which. A size nobody read is left absent; the quotient stands and says so.

A hint is keyed on the EXACT sams_item_id AND the EXACT name. Sam's re-keys items (the Sweet Baby Ray's jug has been 13599611407 and 4W2VMU21D4SI), and a hint that has drifted off its product must stop applying rather than quietly re-size a different jug.

build-sams-deals.ps1 VERIFIES every hint against Sam's own arithmetic before it is used: linePrice / hint must display as the unitPrice Sam's printed (within 0.005001). A reading that fails is reported as BAD HINT in out\sams\sams-rejects-<date>.json and the derived size stands, so a mistyped or mis-united number cannot reach the board.
Exactly ONE size field per entry, and it must be in the unit Sam's priced the row by - a reading in another unit cannot be checked against Sam's arithmetic at all and is reported.

128 fl oz is NOT the answer for a weight-priced gallon. A gallon's weight depends on its density: Sweet Baby Ray's is a 1.3 g/ml sauce, which is why Sam's own arithmetic puts that jug between 159.73 and 184.31 oz.
